selection: step-out from bonsai1/L24/N11621- (10x queue, model pilot: sonnet)

neighbours.label: the verb right after an existential 'there' or a fronted place/time phrase (there will be, there stands, wird/будет): subject-after-verb order, multilingual
fire: Behind the barn there lies a pond nobody has fished in years.
Next month there will be a vote on the new parking rules.
Over the hills there came a sound like distant thunder.
In diesem Gebäude wird künftig ein Museum untergebracht.
В следующем году в городе будет открыт новый парк.
On the shelf there sits a dusty clock that no one winds.
In the report are described the main causes of the delay.
Au sommet de la colline se trouve un vieux moulin.
quiet: The pond lies behind the barn, and nobody has fished in years.
The vote on the new parking rules happens next month.
A sound like distant thunder came over the hills.
Man bringt künftig ein Museum in diesem Gebäude unter.
В следующем году город откроет новый парк.
A dusty clock sits on the shelf, and no one winds it.
The report describes the main causes of the delay.
Le vieux moulin se trouve au sommet de la colline.

notes: Model pilot (sonnet arm; the same pole is tested independently by the other arm, pairing disclosed): this pole feeds the held pole bonsai1/L24/N11621- (zeroing this neuron removes 0.74 of the anchor's peak), from a batched edge measurement with 8 same-layer placebos. Label and all 16 sentences written by the Sonnet 5.5 labeller from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + the edge hint) and one probe round of 8 sentences (none reused). An Opus gate checked rule-level items only and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Probes fired 0.47-0.75 on 'there stands', 'there will', German 'wird' and Russian 'будет'; subject-first versions stayed ~0. 'Is there' scored exactly 0.3 on 'there', so I left questions out except as ordinary subject-first near misses. Pole is broad (many weak activations), so expect noise.
